Hi Natalie / Tom,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As discussed, I put together an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short evaluation cadence so we can align on milestones, commercial triggers, and the residency/failover constraints you called out. The attached PDF is the draft MAP + SOW sketch.

High-level proposal (please confirm if this aligns to your expectations):
- Week 0–2: Sandbox access + baseline performance checks (Redwood assigns dedicated SE).
- Week 3–6: Evaluation POC — we validate 30-day run with sample traffic, measure latency and accuracy on typical request mixes. No charge for up to 50k tokens/day during POC (evaluation credits).
- Milestone A (POC completion): internal sign-off point. If passed, EcomInc receives 5% credit toward month-1 consumption.
- Milestone B (Ramp to committed throughput): Once you commit to a 3-month reserved capacity of X tokens/day, we transition to reserved pricing and apply commit-tier discounts (3–10% depending on ramp).
- Multi-region / data residency: We can host primary/replica in EU+US. There is a data-residency premium for firm EU residency and cross-region failover guarantees — I put an initial premium estimate at ~12% above base list price to cover dedicated region pools, persistent KV cache replication, and higher SLO/retention guarantees.
- Cross-region failover: automatic failover option available for an additional monthly fee; failover preserves encrypted KV caches with a warm standby strategy (expected cold-start delta ~180–350ms depending on model size).

Questions for you before we finalize the MAP:
1) Do you need strict EU-only residency (no egress to US) or is an EU-primary with US failover acceptable with appropriate contractual controls?
2) What number should we use for the committed tokens/day for commercial modeling (ballpark is fine)?
3) Do you want Redwood to include SOC 2 evidence and customer-specific audit logs in the SOW?

Attaching: MAP-EcomInc-v1.pdf (draft), SOW sketch.

If this looks good, Marissa and I will draft the commercial appendix tying commit tiers to the discount schedule and the residency premium.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez

Diego — thanks for the fast follow. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: Our security team requires EU data residency for customer PII. Cross-region failover to US is acceptable only if data-at-rest remains encrypted with customer-managed keys and we have contractual limitations on processing. Can you confirm Redwood supports HSM/KMS with BYOK?
- Premium: 12% is in the right ballpark but finance will want a tiered view: what does 12% cover exactly (storage replication, dedicated instances, higher retention, logs)?
- Discounts tied to commits: we prefer a simple, predictable ramp (e.g., 3-month ramp with step discounts at month 1/2/3) rather than complex usage-based carve-outs.

Sophie from legal is looped in for the residency and encryption ask.

Also — can you share SOC 2 evidence and any region-specific certifications you have? That will accelerate our internal security review.

- EU residency premium breakdown (examples):
  - Dedicated region pools: +7%
  - Persistent KV/cache replication + SLA: +3%
  - Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration and additional audit retention: +2%
  => Total illustrative premium: +12% (we can show alternatives if you'd prefer shared-but-isolated tenancy for lower premium).

- Commit & discount proposal (simple 3-step ramp):
  - Month 1 (post-POC): commit to 0.25M tokens/day for 3 months -> immediate 3% discount off base list.
  - Month 2: increase to 0.5M tokens/day -> additional 3% (cumulative 6%).
  - Month 3+: 1.0M tokens/day -> additional 4% (cumulative 10%).
  - Early acceleration credit: if 1.0M/day reached before month 3, apply back-dated credit to month 1 usage for the delta.

- Cross-region failover commercial terms:
  - Warm-standby failover included as optional add-on priced at a fixed monthly fee (covers reserved capacity in secondary region and replication bandwidth). If you choose autopassive failover (no warm caching), the standby fee is lower but expected cold-start impact is higher.

- Invoice/commit triggers: Finance will be invoiced monthly based on committed capacity. Overages billed at on-demand list rates unless you convert to a higher commit tier mid-term.

Hi all — quick technical clarifications to align expectations for the failover/residency pricing above:

- BYOK/KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations (we can do AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed key stores). We persist only ciphertext and key references in our control plane; key operations are performed via your KMS endpoints — this meets the requirement for customer-managed encryption in most contracts.
- KV/cache replication: to maintain warm failover we replicate compacted KV checkpoints from primary -> replica in near real-time. That uses reserved bandwidth and extra storage (basis for the premium). Replication frequency is configurable (near real-time down to 5s checkpoints).
- Failover SLOs: for warm-standby we target median failover delta <250ms for small models but up to ~350ms for larger families (e.g., 30B+). If you choose cold-start standby, expect 800–1500ms impact on first requests while the cache warms.
- Audit logs & evidence: we can provide per-request metadata (region, model-version, route) in your audit exports; retention is configurable in the SOW appendix.

I'll drop a short architecture diagram to the shared drive. See: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Map-EcomInc

—Karthik
